blocks.content: This appendix builds on Chapter 8, presenting additional results from matrix algebra and linear models. We start by introducing two useful matrix transforms, generalized inverses (for solving singular systems of equations) and the square root of a matrix (for obtaining a set of uncorrelated variables). These results are then used for a formal derivation of several properties of generalized least-squares (GLS) estimators. We next examine how linear model sums of squares can be written as quadratic forms and how these sums of squares are used in formal hypothesis testing. We conclude with two additional topics, equivalent linear models (which allow calculations for one model to be performed on a potentially much simpler model) and a brief introduction to matrix derivatives.
